hook_text: A bag of shapes and two questions. Every shape finds its place, except one troublemaker.
clip_script: Tip out the bag. Question one: straight sides or curved? Triangles, squares, hexagons: straight. Circles: curved. Then the troublemaker, a semicircle. One straight side, one curved. It needs its own group: both. Question two: how many sides? All the three-siders together, all the four-siders together. A tall thin triangle and a wide flat triangle are family. Compare the square and the rectangle: same four straight sides, same square corners, but only the square has all sides equal. Now draw. Grid paper, 3 by 3 square: count three squares along, not three lines, three squares up, join along the grid. One slanted side on a triangle? That one gets the ruler. Two questions, one place for every shape, and always say why.
visual_style: Whiteboard shapes sliding into three labelled columns with a semicircle hovering before a third column appears; a grid with squares counted and highlighted.
pacing: The sort with the semicircle surprise, the compare, then the grid drawing and the line-versus-square tip.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort the shapes in your kitchen drawer by straight and curved.
